tools.name: post_v1_posts
tools.description:
Publish or schedule a multi-target post

Publish a single body to up to 25 connected accounts in one call, or schedule the whole batch for a future time.

- **Multi-target only:** the v1 wire shape requires `targets[]`. The legacy `account: {}` single-target shape is no longer accepted.
- **Idempotent:** include `Idempotency-Key`. Replays within 24 hours return the original response.
- **Preflight:** every documented platform constraint runs locally before the upstream call. Cheap shape preflight is atomic across the batch — if any target fails the synchronous checks the whole call is rejected as `400 preflight_failed`. Deep checks (URL reachability, MIME sniffing, byte caps) run per target and surface inside `results[i].error`, producing a `partial_failed` batch rather than a 400.
- **Errors:** failures use the [stable error envelope](https://letmepost.dev/docs/errors/) — `code`, `rule`, `platformResponse`, `remediation`, `docUrl`, `ruleUrl`.

For per-platform payload differences, see the [platforms guides](https://letmepost.dev/docs/platforms/bluesky/).

items.description: One target on a multi-target publish. Carries an `accountId`, a `platform` hint, or both (must agree). Per-target `text` / `media` / `firstComment` / `options` override the top-level defaults.

accountId.description: letmepost platform_account id. When omitted, `platform` must be set and the org must have exactly one connected account for that platform.

allOf.description: Supported platforms. `tiktok` is currently in App Review — connect requests return `platform_not_enabled` until approval lands.

platform.description: Auto-resolve hint. Used alone when the org has exactly one connected account for the platform; combined with `accountId` it must agree (else `targets.account.platform_mismatch`).

text.description: Per-target text override. Falls back to the top-level `text`.

items.description: A single media item attached to a post. Exactly one of `mediaId` / `url` / `bytesBase64` must be present.

altText.description: Per-platform alt-text caps apply (e.g. Bluesky 2000, Twitter 1000).

mediaId.description: References a previous `POST /v1/media` upload. Preferred for production — bytes already live on our CDN.

url.description: Public URL we fetch from your CDN at publish time. Must respond 200 to anonymous GET.

bytesBase64.description: Inline base64. Convenient for tiny images and tests; use `POST /v1/media` for anything substantial.

media.description: Per-target media override. Falls back to the top-level `media`.

allOf.description: Auto-posted reply to the published post. Bluesky-only today; ignored on platforms that don't support it.

options.description: Per-target platform options. Discriminated on `platform`; the discriminator must match the resolved account's platform or the request fails with `targets.options.platform_mismatch`. Replaces the v0 top-level `pinterest` / `threads` / `twitter` keys.

quoteTweetId.description: Quote this tweet id. Mutually exclusive with `replyToTweetId` — X rejects tweets that combine the two.

boardId.description: Pinterest board to pin to. Falls back to the account's default board when omitted.

destinationUrl.description: Outbound link attached to the pin.

coverImageUrl.description: Cover image URL for video pins.

replyToId.description: Threads thread id to reply under.

text.description: Default text applied to any target that omits its own `text`.

items.description: A single media item attached to a post. Exactly one of `mediaId` / `url` / `bytesBase64` must be present.

altText.description: Per-platform alt-text caps apply (e.g. Bluesky 2000, Twitter 1000).

mediaId.description: References a previous `POST /v1/media` upload. Preferred for production — bytes already live on our CDN.

url.description: Public URL we fetch from your CDN at publish time. Must respond 200 to anonymous GET.

bytesBase64.description: Inline base64. Convenient for tiny images and tests; use `POST /v1/media` for anything substantial.

media.description: Default media applied to any target that omits its own `media`.

firstComment.description: Auto-posted reply to the published post. Bluesky-only today; ignored on platforms that don't support it.

publishNow.description: Explicit immediate-publish mode. Mutually exclusive with `scheduledAt` (`mode_conflict`). When neither is set the request publishes immediately.

scheduledAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp at least 1 second in the future. When set, every target row is queued and the response is 202. Scheduled posts currently accept text only — media and firstComment require an immediate publish.

profileId.description: Profile scope for this batch. Use to target a specific workspace when the API key or OAuth token is org-wide. Forbidden when the key is already scoped to a different profile (rule `profile.scope_mismatch`). Omit to fall back to the key's bound profile.

tools.name: get_v1_posts
tools.description:
List posts (post log)

Cursor-paginated post log scoped to the caller's organization (and profile, when the key is profile-scoped). Filters compose. Array filters (`platform`, `status`, `errorCode`) accept either repeated query params or comma-separated single values.

items.description: Supported platforms. `tiktok` is currently in App Review — connect requests return `platform_not_enabled` until approval lands.
Lifecycle state of a single per-target post row. `canceled` is the terminal state reached via `DELETE /v1/posts/{id}` on a queued scheduled post.

tools.name: get_v1_posts_by_id
tools.description:
Fetch a single post with its publish attempts

Returns the post row plus every publish attempt (start/finish, success flag, upstream response, error code). Use the `postId` returned in `CreatePostResponse.results[]` as `{id}`.

tools.name: patch_v1_posts_by_id
tools.description:
Reschedule a queued post

Move a scheduled post to a new firing time. Only allowed when `status=queued` AND `scheduledAt` is still in the future — once a post enters `publishing` or any terminal state, the window closes and the request returns `409`.

The operation is atomic: the API replaces the BullMQ job (removes the old delayed job, enqueues a new one at the updated delay) and only persists the new `scheduledAt` if the queue swap succeeded. A `post.rescheduled` webhook fires on success, carrying both the old and new timestamps.

scheduledAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone. Must be at least 1 second in the future.

tools.name: delete_v1_posts_by_id
tools.description:
Cancel a queued scheduled post

Cancel a scheduled post before it fires. Only allowed when `status=queued` AND `scheduledAt` is still in the future — same window as `PATCH`. Removes the BullMQ job and transitions the row to `status=canceled`. A `post.canceled` webhook fires on success.

If a worker is already processing the job when cancellation lands, the worker's conditional `UPDATE … WHERE status IN ('queued','validated')` short-circuits and the publish never happens.

tools.name: get_v1_media
tools.description:
List uploaded media

Cursor-paginated. Scoped to the caller's organization, and (when the key is profile-scoped) to that profile. Org-wide keys may narrow with `?profileId=`.

tools.name: get_v1_accounts
tools.description:
List connected accounts

Lists every connected platform account in the caller's organization. No secrets ever leak — display name, platform identifiers, and lifecycle timestamps only.

profileId.description: Narrow to a single profile. Malformed values match nothing rather than 400 (preserves the dashboard's profile-switcher contract).

tools.name: get_v1_accounts_by_id
tools.description: Fetch a connected account

tools.name: delete_v1_accounts_by_id
tools.description:
Disconnect (hard delete)

Dashboard session only — programmatic keys cannot disconnect accounts. Hard delete: the platform_accounts row is removed and any persisted token is destroyed.

tools.name: post_v1_accounts_connect_by_platform
tools.description:
Start a connect flow

Dashboard session only. Returns a `ConnectDescriptor` describing how to finish the connect — an OAuth authorization URL for OAuth platforms, or a credentials form schema for Bluesky. Programmatic API keys cannot mint OAuth state.

platform.description: Supported platforms. `tiktok` is currently in App Review — connect requests return `platform_not_enabled` until approval lands.

profileId.description: Land the resulting account in this profile. Falls back to the org's default profile when omitted.

tools.name: post_v1_accounts_connect_by_platform_complete
tools.description:
Finish a connect flow

Dashboard session only. Completes the handshake started by `POST /v1/accounts/connect/{platform}` — for OAuth platforms this is invoked from the redirect callback flow; for credentials platforms (Bluesky) it carries the credentials in the body. Upserts the platform_accounts row (re-connecting the same account rotates the stored token rather than 409-ing).

platform.description: Supported platforms. `tiktok` is currently in App Review — connect requests return `platform_not_enabled` until approval lands.

tools.name: get_v1_accounts_by_id_pinterest_boards
tools.description:
List Pinterest boards on a connected account

Proxy to Pinterest's `/v5/boards` using the stored token. Used by the dashboard's default-board picker so a user can see their actual boards.

tools.name: post_v1_accounts_by_id_pinterest_boards
tools.description:
Create a Pinterest board

Creates a board on the user's Pinterest account without sending them off-site. Optional `setAsDefault` lifts the new board id into the account's default in one round-trip. Optional `upsert: true` returns the existing board (with `existing: true`) on duplicate-name instead of 409-ing.

setAsDefault.description: Lift the new board id into `tokenMetadata.defaultBoardId`.

upsert.description: When true, a duplicate-name response from Pinterest resolves to a 200 with the existing board (`existing: true`) instead of a `platform_rejected` failure.

tools.name: patch_v1_accounts_by_id_pinterest_default_board
tools.description:
Set the default Pinterest board for publishes

Persists the supplied `boardId` as the account's default — used when a `POST /v1/posts` body omits `options.boardId` for a Pinterest target. The board is validated against the account's own boards list before persisting.

tools.name: post_v1_api_keys
tools.description:
Mint an API key

Dashboard session only. The plaintext `key` is returned **once** in this response and never again — store it securely. Optional `profileId` pins the key to a single profile; cross-profile reads/writes 404 under that key.

profileId.description: Optional profile scope. When set, the key only authenticates requests targeting that profile; cross-profile reads/writes 404.

tools.name: get_v1_api_keys
tools.description:
List API keys

Dashboard session only. Plaintext is never returned again — only `last4` and metadata.

tools.name: delete_v1_api_keys_by_id
tools.description:
Revoke an API key

Soft-revoke. The key is invalidated immediately; the row stays for audit. Already-revoked keys 404.

tools.name: post_v1_webhook_endpoints
tools.description:
Register a webhook endpoint

Dashboard session only. The `signingSecret` is returned **once** at creation — used to verify the HMAC-SHA256 `X-Letmepost-Signature` header on every delivery. An empty `events` array subscribes to every event type.

events.description: Empty array subscribes the endpoint to every event type.

tools.name: get_v1_webhook_endpoints
tools.description: List webhook endpoints

tools.name: get_v1_webhook_endpoints_by_id
tools.description: Fetch a webhook endpoint

tools.name: patch_v1_webhook_endpoints_by_id
tools.description:
Update a webhook endpoint

Partial update. Setting `active: false` pauses delivery without losing the endpoint; flipping back to `true` re-enables it.

tools.name: delete_v1_webhook_endpoints_by_id
tools.description:
Delete a webhook endpoint

Hard delete — the row is removed. Use `PATCH … { active: false }` instead if you want to pause delivery while preserving history.

tools.name: post_v1_webhook_endpoints_by_id_test
tools.description:
Send a synthetic test delivery

Fires a synthetic event at the endpoint URL synchronously and returns what the consumer responded — bypasses the BullMQ delivery queue on purpose so operators get immediate feedback. The real signing secret is used; the consumer's HMAC verification path is identical to production.
